title: 1st Tyrolean Wood Museum Wildschönau
name: 1st Tyrolean Wood Museum Wildschönau
kurzbeschreibung: The 1st Tyrolean Wood Museum in Auffach in the Wildschönau: over 3,000 fascinating wooden exhibits in the rustic birthplace of woodcarver Hubert Salcher.
beschreibung:
Overview

The multi-award-winning 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum is located in the picturesque mountain village of Auffach in the rear high valley of the Wildschönau (Kufstein district) at an altitude of around 875 meters above sea level. Framed by the wildly romantic peaks of the Kitzbüheler Alpen, this private cultural museum is housed in a heritage-listed timber block farmhouse over 300 years old. Created by the renowned Wildschönau sculptor and woodcarver Hubert Salcher, the museum presents a collection unique in Europe that brings to life the universal significance of wood throughout Tyrolean cultural history.

Collection, Craftsmanship & Curiosities

Spread across two floors and more than thirty rustic parlors and chambers, the museum gathers more than 3,000 fascinating exhibits made entirely of wood. The spectrum ranges from centuries-old peasant farming tools, hand-carved wooden clogs, sleds, and cradles to intricate wooden clocks, musical instruments, and delicate artistic woodcarvings. Among the curious highlights are Tyrol's oldest wooden washing machine, a collection of hand-whittled wooden nails, and masterfully crafted stone pine sculptures. The museum's founder often guides guests personally through the rooms and demonstrates traditional woodturning and carving techniques in his open workshop. For the senses, the house offers an unparalleled experience: the intense, soothing scent of aged Swiss stone pine, spruce, and larch wood permeates every corner of the historic timber dwelling.

Visit & Getting There

The 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum is open during the summer season from early May to mid-October from Wednesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays and Tuesdays; special opening days during the winter season). Admission fees (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults approx. €8.00, seniors approx. €7.00, children (6 to 15 years) approx. €4.00, small children free; family ticket approx. €18.00. Holders of the regional Wildschönau Card enjoy free admission! Getting there by car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl Ost), continuing along the Wildschönauer Landesstraße L3 via Niederau and Oberau for around 15 kilometers to Auffach; the museum is well signposted in the hamlet of Dorf (free parking on site). By public transport: ÖBB train to Wörgl station, followed by Postbus line 4064 directly to the stop Auffach Holzmuseum.

Tips

The ground floor is largely accessible with low barriers; a traditional wooden staircase leads to the upper parlors. Take the opportunity in the adjoining museum shop to acquire hand-carved Swiss stone pine creations, fragrant stone pine pillows, and original wooden gifts directly from the master carver. Pair your visit with a ride on the nearby Schatzbergbahn cable car up into the world of alpine pastures.
